Osteoarthritis Knee Pain: Don’t Ignore the Warning Signs

Osteoarthritis is one of the most common causes of knee pain, especially after 40. It occurs when the protective cartilage in the knee joint gradually wears down, leading to pain, stiffness, and reduced movement.

Common Symptoms:
• Pain while walking or climbing stairs
• Morning stiffness in the knee
• Swelling or tenderness
• Cracking or grinding sensation (crepitus)
• Reduced flexibility and difficulty in movement

Causes:
• Age-related wear and tear
• Excess body weight (increased joint stress)
• Sedentary lifestyle
• Previous knee injury
• Weak muscles around the knee

Treatment & Care:
Early intervention can slow down the progression of osteoarthritis. Physiotherapy helps reduce pain, improve joint mobility, and strengthen supporting muscles. Lifestyle changes, guided exercises, and advanced therapies can significantly improve your quality of life.

Remember - knee pain may be common, but it is not normal.

Knee Meniscus Tear: Don’t Ignore the Early Signs

A meniscus tear is one of the most common knee injuries, especially in people who are active or above 40. It happens when the cushioning cartilage in your knee gets damaged due to sudden twisting, squatting, or age-related wear and tear.

Common Symptoms:
• Pain while walking or climbing stairs
• Swelling or stiffness in the knee
• Locking or catching sensation
• Difficulty in fully bending or straightening the knee

Causes:
• Sudden twist or turn during activity
• Deep squatting or heavy lifting
• Sports injuries
• Age-related degeneration of knee cartilage

Treatment & Care:
Early treatment can prevent the condition from worsening. Physiotherapy plays a key role in recovery by reducing pain, improving mobility, and strengthening the muscles around the knee.
In many cases, surgery can be avoided with the right exercises and timely care.
